README.md-1-# Serverless Shopping Cart Microservice
README.md-2-
README.md:3:This application is a sample application to demonstrate how you could implement a shopping cart microservice using 
README.md:4:serverless technologies on AWS. The backend is built as a REST API interface, making use of [Amazon API Gateway](https://aws.amazon.com/api-gateway/), [AWS Lambda](https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/), [Amazon Cognito](https://aws.amazon.com/cognito/), and [Amazon DynamoDB](https://aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/). The frontend is a Vue.js application using the [AWS Amplify](https://aws-amplify.github.io/) SDK for authentication and communication with the API.

README.md-14-## Design Notes
README.md-15-
README.md:16:Before building the application, I set some requirements on how the cart should behave:
README.md-17-
README.md:18:- Users should be able to add items to the cart without logging in (an "anonymous cart"), and that cart should persist 
README.md-19-across browser restarts etc.
README.md:20:- When logging in, if there were products in an anonymous cart, they should be added to the user's cart from any 
README.md-21-previous logged in sessions.
README.md:22:- When logging out, the anonymous cart should not have products in it any longer.
README.md:23:- Items in an anonymous cart should be removed after a period of time, and items in a logged in cart should persist 
README.md-24-for a longer period.
README.md:25:- Admin users to be able to get an aggregated view of the total number of each product in users' carts at any time.
README.md-26-
README.md-27-### Cart Migration
README.md-28-
README.md:29:When an item is added to the cart, an item is written in DynamoDB with an identifier which matches a randomly generated 
README.md:30:(uuid) cookie which is set in the browser. This allows a user to add items to cart and come back to the page later 
README.md-31-without losing the items they have added. When the user logs in, these items will be removed, and replaced with items 
README.md:32:with a user id as the pk. If the user already had that product in their cart from a previous logged in session, the 
README.md-33-quantities would be summed. Because we don't need the deletion of old items to happen immediately as part of a 
README.md-34-synchronous workflow, we put messages onto an SQS queue, which triggers a worker function to delete the messages.  
README.md-35-
README.md:36:To expire items from users' shopping carts, DynamoDB's native functionality is used where a TTL is written along with 
README.md-37-the item, after which the item should be removed. In this implementation, the TTL defaults to 1 day for anonymous 
README.md:38:carts, and 7 days for logged in carts.  
README.md-39-
README.md:40:### Aggregated View of Products in Carts
README.md-41-
README.md:42:It would be possible to scan our entire DynamoDB table and sum up the quantities of all the products, but this will be 
README.md-43-expensive past a certain scale. Instead, we can calculate the total as a running process, and keep track of the total 
README.md-44-amount.  
README.md-45-
README.md:46:When an item is added, deleted or updated in DynamoDB, an event is put onto DynamoDB Streams, which in turn triggers a 
README.md:47:Lambda function. This function calculates the change in total quantity for each product in users' carts, and writes the 
README.md:48:quantity back to DynamoDB. The Lambda function is configured so that it will run after either 60 seconds pass, or 100 
README.md-49-new events are on the stream. This would enable an admin user to get real time data about the popular products, which 
README.md-50-could in turn help anticipate inventory. In this implementation, the API is exposed without authentication to

README.md-56-### Shopping Cart Service
README.md-57-
README.md-58-GET  
README.md:59:`/cart`  
README.md:60:Retrieves the shopping cart for a user who is either anonymous or logged in.  
README.md-61-
README.md-62-POST  
README.md:63:`/cart`  
README.md:64:Accepts a product id and quantity as json. Adds specified quantity of an item to cart.  
README.md-65-
README.md:66:`/cart/migrate`  
README.md:67:Called after logging in - migrates items in an anonymous user's cart to belong to their logged in user. If you already 
README.md:68:have a cart on your logged in user, your "anonymous cart" will be merged with it when you log in.
README.md-69-
README.md:70:`/cart/checkout`  
README.md:71:Currently just empties cart.
README.md-72-
README.md-73-PUT  
README.md:74:`/cart/{product-id}`  
README.md-75-Accepts a product id and quantity as json. Updates quantity of given item to provided quantity.  
README.md-76-
README.md-77-GET  
README.md:78:`/cart/{product-id}/total`  
README.md:79:Returns the total amount of a given product across all carts. This API is not used by the frontend but can be manually 
README.md-80-called to test.

     1	# Serverless Shopping Cart Microservice
     2	
     3	This application is a sample application to demonstrate how you could implement a shopping cart microservice using 
     4	serverless technologies on AWS. The backend is built as a REST API interface, making use of [Amazon API Gateway](https://aws.amazon.com/api-gateway/), [AWS Lambda](https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/), [Amazon Cognito](https://aws.amazon.com/cognito/), and [Amazon DynamoDB](https://aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/). The frontend is a Vue.js application using the [AWS Amplify](https://aws-amplify.github.io/) SDK for authentication and communication with the API.
     5	
     6	To assist in demonstrating the functionality, a bare bones mock "products" service has also been included. Since the 
     7	authentication parts are likely to be shared between components, there is a separate template for it. The front-end 
     8	doesn't make any real payment integration at this time.
     9	
    10	## Architecture & Design
    11	
    12	![Architecture Diagram](./images/architecture.png)
    13	
    14	## Design Notes
    15	
    16	Before building the application, I set some requirements on how the cart should behave:
    17	
    18	- Users should be able to add items to the cart without logging in (an "anonymous cart"), and that cart should persist 
    19	across browser restarts etc.
    20	- When logging in, if there were products in an anonymous cart, they should be added to the user's cart from any 
    21	previous logged in sessions.
    22	- When logging out, the anonymous cart should not have products in it any longer.
    23	- Items in an anonymous cart should be removed after a period of time, and items in a logged in cart should persist 
    24	for a longer period.
    25	- Admin users to be able to get an aggregated view of the total number of each product in users' carts at any time.
    26	
    27	### Cart Migration
    28	
    29	When an item is added to the cart, an item is written in DynamoDB with an identifier which matches a randomly generated 
    30	(uuid) cookie which is set in the browser. This allows a user to add items to cart and come back to the page later 
    31	without losing the items they have added. When the user logs in, these items will be removed, and replaced with items 
    32	with a user id as the pk. If the user already had that product in their cart from a previous logged in session, the 
    33	quantities would be summed. Because we don't need the deletion of old items to happen immediately as part of a 
    34	synchronous workflow, we put messages onto an SQS queue, which triggers a worker function to delete the messages.  
    35	
    36	To expire items from users' shopping carts, DynamoDB's native functionality is used where a TTL is written along with 
    37	the item, after which the item should be removed. In this implementation, the TTL defaults to 1 day for anonymous 
    38	carts, and 7 days for logged in carts.  
    39	
    40	### Aggregated View of Products in Carts
    41	
    42	It would be possible to scan our entire DynamoDB table and sum up the quantities of all the products, but this will be 
    43	expensive past a certain scale. Instead, we can calculate the total as a running process, and keep track of the total 
    44	amount.  
    45	
    46	When an item is added, deleted or updated in DynamoDB, an event is put onto DynamoDB Streams, which in turn triggers a 
    47	Lambda function. This function calculates the change in total quantity for each product in users' carts, and writes the 
    48	quantity back to DynamoDB. The Lambda function is configured so that it will run after either 60 seconds pass, or 100 
    49	new events are on the stream. This would enable an admin user to get real time data about the popular products, which 
    50	could in turn help anticipate inventory. In this implementation, the API is exposed without authentication to 
    51	demonstrate the functionality.  
    52	
    53	
    54	## Api Design
    55	
    56	### Shopping Cart Service
    57	
    58	GET  
    59	`/cart`  
    60	Retrieves the shopping cart for a user who is either anonymous or logged in.  
    61	
    62	POST  
    63	`/cart`  
    64	Accepts a product id and quantity as json. Adds specified quantity of an item to cart.  
    65	
    66	`/cart/migrate`  
    67	Called after logging in - migrates items in an anonymous user's cart to belong to their logged in user. If you already 
    68	have a cart on your logged in user, your "anonymous cart" will be merged with it when you log in.
    69	
    70	`/cart/checkout`  
    71	Currently just empties cart.
    72	
    73	PUT  
    74	`/cart/{product-id}`  
    75	Accepts a product id and quantity as json. Updates quantity of given item to provided quantity.  
    76	
    77	GET  
    78	`/cart/{product-id}/total`  
    79	Returns the total amount of a given product across all carts. This API is not used by the frontend but can be manually 
    80	called to test.  
    81	
    82	### Product Mock Service
    83	
    84	GET  
    85	`/product`  
    86	Returns details for all products.  
    87	
    88	`/product/{product_id}`  
    89	Returns details for a single product.

The web client calls the cart migration route after login.

Cart API is the consumer-facing REST boundary for the shopping-cart capability.

# Consumers

[Shopping Cart Web Client](../components/shopping-cart-web-client.md) invokes cart retrieval, additions, updates, migration, and checkout. The total lookup is documented as manually callable rather than used by the frontend.

GET `/cart`; POST `/cart`; PUT `/cart/{product_id}`; POST `/cart/migrate`; POST `/cart/checkout`; and GET `/cart/{product_id}/total` are grouped in this surface.

# Failure Behavior

The inspected source does not specify a common API error contract.

This API is part of [Serverless Shopping Cart](../systems/serverless-shopping-cart.md) and implemented in [aws-serverless-shopping-cart](../repositories/aws-serverless-shopping-cart.md).
